Actually, let me consider: the permission rejection might be a fluke. But the right behavior is to tell the user it was blocked, and not circumvent via shell.

The read was blocked — the tool returned a permission rejection ("Not now"), so I don't have the file's contents to show you.

I won't try to work around that by reading it through the shell, since that would sidestep the same approval you declined.

If it was an accidental dismissal, a couple of options:
- Re-run the request and approve the read prompt when it appears.
- Tell me the specific keys you need (e.g. just the variable names, or non-secret values), and I can suggest how to get them.

One note: `.env` files typically hold credentials, so if you do want me to read it, be aware the values will appear in this conversation.
I'll read the file for you.
